chunks: What was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a woman with whom her husband has intercourse, then she menstruates before performing ghusl. He said: If she wishes to perform ghusl, she may do so; and if she does not do it, then there is nothing upon her. Then when she becomes pure, she performs one ghusl for menstruation and janabah.

key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: the state of janabah caused by sexual intercourse
key_terms.تَغْتَسِلَ: to perform ghusl, the ritual bath

ai.seo_question: If a woman becomes junub and then menstruates before ghusl, does she need one ghusl or two?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a woman who enters the state of janabah and then begins menstruation before performing ghusl. It states that performing ghusl immediately is optional, and after becoming pure from menstruation, one ghusl suffices for both hayd and janabah.
